def Target : Prop :=
  ∃ _ : Theory.RE Def9,
    (∀ K : Def1, Def3 K → ∃ σ, σ ∈ Def9.theory ∧ σ ∉ K) ∧
    (∃ K : Def1, Def6 K ∧ Def3 K ∧ Def8 K ∧ 𝗣𝗔.theory ⊆ K ∧ Def7 Def9 ∈ K)
a_raw: {"translation":"For a recursively enumerable arithmetic axiom set F, let C(F) be the arithmetic sentence saying that falsehood is not provable from the Δ₁ axiom presentation obtained by Craig’s trick from F. Let A be the PA axioms together with the single additional axiom ¬C(PA). Target is the proposition that there is a witness that A is recursively enumerable and, with this witness used to form C(A), both of the following hold. (1) For every set K of arithmetic sentences, if every member of K is true in the standard natural numbers, then there is a sentence σ provable from A that is not a member of K. Here σ may depend on K; K need not be effectively presented or deductively closed, and the conclusion is nonmembership, not unprovability from K. (2) There exists a set K of arithmetic sentences such that there exists a recursively enumerable arithmetic axiom set F whose set of theorems is exactly K; every member of K is true in the standard natural numbers; every sentence provable using K as axioms belongs to K; every theorem of PA belongs to K (not necessarily a strict inclusion); and C(A) belongs to K."}
translation: For a recursively enumerable arithmetic axiom set F, let C(F) be the arithmetic sentence saying that falsehood is not provable from the Δ₁ axiom presentation obtained by Craig’s trick from F. Let A be the PA axioms together with the single additional axiom ¬C(PA). Target is the proposition that there is a witness that A is recursively enumerable and, with this witness used to form C(A), both of the following hold. (1) For every set K of arithmetic sentences, if every member of K is true in the standard natural numbers, then there is a sentence σ provable from A that is not a member of K. Here σ may depend on K; K need not be effectively presented or deductively closed, and the conclusion is nonmembership, not unprovability from K. (2) There exists a set K of arithmetic sentences such that there exists a recursively enumerable arithmetic axiom set F whose set of theorems is exactly K; every member of K is true in the standard natural numbers; every sentence provable using K as axioms belongs to K; every theorem of PA belongs to K (not necessarily a strict inclusion); and C(A) belongs to K.

judgement.summary: The TARGET states both (i) and (ii) for the same system A = PA + ¬Con(PA), using Craig presentations for the consistency sentences. Applying (i) to the sound mind K from (ii) gives an A-theorem outside K even though Con(A) belongs to K, contradicting the set-level implication without making any claim about DTK.
